name: Component Gallery Comparative Research Wave 2
policy: Use public taxonomy, counts, guidance and behavior principles as cross-system research. Do not copy screenshots, branded visual expression, proprietary code or exact compositions. Verify the originating design system license before source reuse.

components.purpose: A text input combined with a popup option collection so users can filter or search a predefined set while retaining keyboard selection behavior.
keyboardModel: Typing filters or searches options
ArrowDown/ArrowUp moves active option
Enter commits the active option
Escape closes the popup without unexpectedly clearing a committed value
Tab follows the host application's focus model
responsiveRules: Keep the text field visible and usable at narrow widths
Popup must remain within viewport bounds
Large result sets need scrolling without trapping the page
On mobile, a full-width or sheet treatment may replace a tiny anchored popup when needed
antiPatterns: Using a combobox when a small static select is sufficient
Treating typed free text as a valid value when the data model requires predefined options
Hiding the current selection
Mouse-only option selection
components.comparativeSignal: Across systems, the key distinction from Select is typed filtering/search plus listbox-style option navigation.

components.purpose: A calendar-oriented control for choosing a valid date, date range or date/time while respecting locale, constraints and typed entry when supported.
keyboardModel: Arrow keys navigate dates according to calendar semantics
Enter/Space selects the focused date
Escape closes an overlay calendar
Month/year movement must remain keyboard reachable
Focus returns predictably to the trigger or date field
responsiveRules: Use enough touch area for calendar cells
Avoid clipped month grids
Range selection must remain understandable on narrow screens
Long month/localized labels must not overflow
Consider full-screen/sheet calendars on small mobile viewports
antiPatterns: Forcing a calendar when direct date entry is faster
Using ambiguous date formats
Allowing unavailable dates to appear selectable
Moving months without announcing context to assistive technology
components.comparativeSignal: The gallery shows calendar, range-calendar, scrollable calendar, appointment-picker and datetime variants; the task and constraints should choose the model rather than styling preference.

components.purpose: A trigger-controlled menu of actions or navigation choices; unlike Select, it is not primarily a form value input.
keyboardModel: Enter/Space opens from a button trigger
Arrow keys navigate menu items
Enter/Space activates the focused action
Escape closes and restores trigger focus
Submenus follow directional keyboard conventions
responsiveRules: Keep popup inside viewport
Provide sufficient item hit targets
Long labels may wrap only when it does not destroy scanability
For complex mobile menus, promote to a sheet/drawer rather than an unusably small floating menu
antiPatterns: Using it as a form Select
Putting arbitrary form layouts inside a menu role
Using hover as the only way to open
Making disabled actions look enabled
components.comparativeSignal: Component Gallery explicitly separates Dropdown Menu from Select because one exposes actions/navigation and the other commits form values.

components.purpose: Switch between related content panels while keeping all panels at the same information level.
keyboardModel: Arrow keys move among tabs according to orientation
Home/End may move to first/last tab
Selected tab controls a corresponding tabpanel
Focus behavior must follow manual or automatic activation deliberately
responsiveRules: Do not shrink labels below readability
Use horizontal scroll or an intentional alternate navigation at narrow widths
Keep selected state visible when tab list scrolls
Do not silently turn tabs into unrelated accordion semantics unless the information architecture allows it
antiPatterns: Using tabs for sequential steps
Using tabs for unrelated destinations
Hiding critical content behind many tabs
Mouse-only tab changes
components.comparativeSignal: With 80 examples, tabs are widely implemented, but correct keyboard/tabpanel semantics are more important than the underline/pill visual treatment.

components.purpose: Transient layered feedback for a completed or failed action without blocking the primary task.
keyboardModel: Any action inside the toast must be keyboard reachable
Dismiss control must have an accessible name
Focus should not be stolen for routine informational toasts
responsiveRules: Toast stack must not obscure primary mobile controls
Long messages should wrap without covering the whole viewport
Respect safe areas
Limit concurrent toasts and preserve reading time
antiPatterns: Using a toast for information the user must review before continuing
Auto-dismissing critical errors too quickly
Stacking unlimited notifications
Using color alone to communicate severity
components.comparativeSignal: The gallery treats Toast as layered transient feedback; persistent or blocking information belongs in Alert or Dialog patterns.

components.purpose: Provide concise supplementary information associated with an element without becoming the main interactive surface.
keyboardModel: Tooltip must be available from keyboard focus as well as pointer hover
Escape may dismiss a visible tooltip
Tooltip content must not require pointer-only interaction
responsiveRules: Do not depend on hover on touch devices
Keep content short and within viewport
If content needs controls or lengthy explanation, promote to Popover or inline help
antiPatterns: Putting buttons or links inside a tooltip
Using tooltip for essential labels
Showing important validation only in a tooltip
Hover-only access
components.comparativeSignal: Component Gallery relates Tooltip to Popover but distinguishes it by concise non-primary information and lack of an interactive content surface.

components.purpose: Show interactive contextual content anchored to a trigger without necessarily blocking interaction with the rest of the page.
keyboardModel: Enter/Space opens from a button trigger
Escape closes and restores trigger focus
Interactive descendants are keyboard reachable
Modal versus non-modal focus behavior must be decided explicitly
responsiveRules: Flip or shift to remain on-screen
Keep content concise
For complex mobile content, use a sheet/drawer/dialog
Avoid internal scrolling unless necessary
antiPatterns: Using the trigger for a second unrelated action
Putting critical always-needed information only in a popover
Failing to return focus
Treating a modal popover as non-modal or vice versa
components.comparativeSignal: The gallery explicitly notes that popovers may contain interactive elements and are commonly click-triggered, unlike ordinary tooltips.

components.purpose: Navigate or manipulate nested hierarchical data such as filesystems, taxonomies or organizational structures.
keyboardModel: ArrowUp/ArrowDown moves visible-node focus
ArrowRight expands or moves into children
ArrowLeft collapses or moves to parent
Enter/Space activates or selects according to the product model
Home/End support should be considered for long trees
responsiveRules: Preserve hierarchy at narrow widths
Avoid uncontrolled indentation that destroys content width
Large trees need filtering/search and virtualization where appropriate
Touch expand controls must be distinct from node activation when both exist
antiPatterns: Using a tree for flat data
Using an accordion when hierarchical navigation/selection is required
Icons that add clutter without differentiating node types
Expansion state with no visible indicator
components.comparativeSignal: Component Gallery warns against tree views for non-hierarchical data and points to dedicated ARIA tree semantics for keyboard interaction.

components.purpose: Browse a bounded sequence of related slides or media items when showing all items at once would be impractical.
keyboardModel: Visible previous/next controls are keyboard operable
Slide changes must not unexpectedly move focus
Autoplay must be pausable
Inactive content should not create confusing tab stops
responsiveRules: Support swipe/scroll without requiring gesture-only controls
Use logical properties and scroll snapping where appropriate
Keep navigation controls visible
Respect reduced motion
Ensure partially visible slides do not imply inaccessible content
antiPatterns: Hiding primary content in an auto-advancing carousel
Gesture-only navigation
Autoplay without pause
Using carousel when a simple grid/list gives better discoverability
components.comparativeSignal: The gallery emphasizes discoverability, on-screen controls, hiding inactive content appropriately and respecting motion preferences.

components.purpose: Provide structured links for moving between pages, views or meaningful regions within the current page.
keyboardModel: Normal navigation links remain reachable in document order
Current destination is conveyed semantically
Disclosure-based mobile/mega navigation has explicit trigger state
Escape closes temporary navigation overlays and restores focus when appropriate
responsiveRules: Choose horizontal, vertical, rail, bottom, side or in-page navigation from the information architecture
Mobile navigation must preserve priority rather than simply hide everything behind one menu
Long labels and localization must be accommodated
Active destination remains visible
antiPatterns: Using application-menu keyboard semantics for ordinary site navigation links without reason
Hiding critical destinations on mobile
Multiple unlabeled navigation landmarks
Treating tabs, menus and navigation as interchangeable because they look similar
components.comparativeSignal: The 62 examples span app bars, side navigation, bottom navigation, rails, jump links, primary/secondary navigation and mega menus; the information architecture should select the pattern.

crossComponentHardRules: Combobox is not merely a styled Select: typed filtering/search changes its interaction and state model.
Dropdown Menu exposes actions or navigation; Select commits form values.
Tooltip is supplementary and non-interactive; Popover may contain interactive contextual content.
Tabs represent peer panels; Stepper represents sequence/progress; Navigation moves among destinations.
Toast is transient feedback; Alert is persistent/prominent feedback; Modal/Alert Dialog blocks or focuses the task.
Tree View is hierarchical; Accordion is disclosure-oriented; a flat List should remain a List.
Carousel is not a default way to hide overflow; use it only when sequential browsing is a real task.
Datepicker must encode locale and date constraints, not just render a calendar grid.
